statement: Storage, as used in the estimate, is the amount of space required to store the data; for the online/offline indicator it is tiny because only two integers per user are stored.
detail: Stated while concluding that storage is not the challenge for this system (8 GB even for a billion users); sets up the later contrast that the challenge is something else (computation, picked up in part 2).
speaker: teacher
verbatim: Storage is the amount of space you require to store the data. Because all we are doing is two integers we are storing.

statement: A common misconception today is that everything has to be a service; a connection pool is not one, it is a library inside the API server.
detail: The teacher's aside while explaining where the connection pool runs: 'For some reason, nowadays, everyone thinks everything is a service. No.' K2-025 makes the factual point (pool = library in the API server) and keeps this remark only in its detail. This item records the misconception the teacher pushes back on.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: So connection pool is not a service. For some reason, nowadays, everyone thinks everything is a service. No.

statement: The point of the find-all-caching-places exercise is to spark ideas and help students understand the many interesting, quote-unquote, hacks people have applied to get the maximum performance out of their systems.
